decision.title: XML parsing speed: fewer tokens and nodes (packet )

body.p: , after , , , . tree-sitter stays the parser (, the owner's choice); the grammar and its external scanner stay the one source of the lexical rules; 's segments are kept.

item.p: Profile (callgrind, sxml check of a 10.5 MB document made of three copies of the XMark auction): 6.7 x 10^9 instructions, 640 a byte, about 1.3 million tokens. Three quarters were tree-sitter's work per token and per node: lexing 29 % (the lexer's advance per character 9 %), the parse stack and subtrees, and 11 % rebalancing the repeat of a content segment's items after each parse; the walk 22 % (field lookups by name, node types by string, a cursor per tag). The cost is per token and node, not per character, so the change cuts tokens and nodes.

Grammar (grammars/xml, README contract updated): a tag's '<' and its name are one external token; '<a>', '<a/>' and a whole end tag '</a S?>' are one token each, nodes without children (start_tag, empty_element_tag, end_tag), and an attribute whose value holds no reference is one token, Name Eq AttValue, an attribute without children ([40] to [44], [41], [25], [10]). The scanner still checks every end tag against its start (WFC: Element Type Match) and every character ([2] Char); a value with a reference, a '<' or a bad character falls back to the grammar's own rules. The items of a content segment are a left-recursive hidden rule rather than a repeat, which tree-sitter does not rebalance (right recursion was slower). The helper rules that choose the token or the full rule are inlined, saving a reduction per tag.

Builder (src/xml.c): the tag name is read past the '<' up to the first '>', '/' or S, and a one-token attribute is split at its first S or '=' and its quotes, none of which a Name holds; fields by number (the language is checked before each parse to number its fields as sxml_xml_field_texts lists them); node types from a table of the language's symbols filled per parse; no child cursor for a tag without children. The segment cut scan uses memchr; the position tracker counts lines and columns in place for UTF-8 and US-ASCII; sxml_utf8_validate passes eight ASCII bytes at a time.
Measured (instructions x 10^9, exact; seconds are processor time, fastest of three, on a machine other builds share), at ceacfa3 without and with the change:

Each change, check of 10.5 MB: tag tokens 6.715 to 5.941; content items left-recursive 5.409; attribute values as tokens 5.211 (later folded into whole attributes); fields by number 5.100; node types by symbol and memchr 4.906; scanner ASCII paths 4.786; no cursor for childless tags 4.687; tags without children 4.210; whole attributes 3.969; UTF-8 validation by words 3.901 (byte by byte was slower). The tracker: building the tree 5.363 to 5.220. Segments () of 4 KB and 64 KB: 4.982 and 4.968; 16 KB kept. Resident memory unchanged. Parsing is now 16 % of XMark-All (25 % before).

Behaviour: the same documents are accepted and refused, with the same events and positions; a syntax error inside a tag may be located a few bytes away (at the tag's '<' rather than at its name). Tests: debug 378/378, xmlconf (xml_conformance), the grammar corpus 67/67, xml_parse_fuzz seeds and 3 minutes clean; QT4 and XT40 whole, release, case by case: no outcome changes (XP40 32,655, XQ40 45,914, XT40 11,913 passed).

Left: what remains is tree-sitter's own cost per token (the lexer's advance per character, the stack, subtree allocation, the tree's deletion) and per character data item, which only fewer tokens or a change of the runtime (vendored unmodified) would reduce; a long character data or attribute token still passes the lexer a character at a time.
